problem_summary.summary: Decide whether every opening bracket is closed by the same type in the correct nested order.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: a string containing only (), {}, and []. Return true exactly when all brackets match and the string is fully balanced.
constraints: s contains only the six bracket characters ()[]{}

brute_force.explanation: Repeatedly remove adjacent matching bracket pairs from a working string. When no pair remains, the input is valid exactly if the working string is empty.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Every valid bracket string contains an innermost adjacent matching pair. Removing such a pair preserves validity; conversely, repeated removal to empty certifies that all brackets were paired in properly nested order.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n^2) in the worst case because several full passes may be needed as inner pairs are removed.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) for the current and next strings.

optimized.explanation: Push each opening bracket. For a closing bracket, require the stack top to be its matching opener and pop it; any mismatch fails immediately.
optimized.correctness_idea: The most recently opened unmatched bracket must close first. Therefore, the stack top is the only valid match for each closing bracket; an empty stack at the end means every opener was matched.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n), with one pass over the string.
optimized.space_complexity: O(n) for the stack of unmatched opening brackets.

steps.condition: Each closer matches the current stack top.

edge_cases.case: A closer appears before any opener
edge_cases.handling: The optimized implementation returns false when the stack is empty.

edge_cases.case: Correct characters but wrong nesting, such as ([)]
edge_cases.handling: The most recent opener does not match the closer, so validation fails.
A nonempty stack makes the final result false.
